claims_about_writeup.why: The write-up (submission/contribution.md) runs to approximately this length (~290 words by direct count), so the stated word count is accurate.

message_source_quote: The repo's reading list contains White-Bear Steering (raman2026) — an existing method in exactly this setup (think/don't-think stance direction, band L20–24, large dose; 0.83 on their split). I reproduced its recipe as a diagnostic control (0.42 on this dev-fit split, confirming the server's position/dose semantics: `prefix` = all positions up to and including the read cell, `read` = read cell only) and used it as a reference, then searched for a new contrast, since the task forbids reproductions.
writeup_source_quote: Not a stance direction (White-Bear Steering: think vs don't-think about a named concept over a neutral sentence), nor an attitude vector (Herrera 2026, negative result).

differences.what: Whether an actual reproduction of White-Bear Steering was run as a diagnostic control, with its own score
differences.message_quote: I reproduced its recipe as a diagnostic control (0.42 on this dev-fit split, confirming the server's position/dose semantics: `prefix` = all positions up to and including the read cell, `read` = read cell only) and used it as a reference, then searched for a new contrast, since the task forbids reproductions.
differences.writeup_quote: Not a stance direction (White-Bear Steering: think vs don't-think about a named concept over a neutral sentence), nor an attitude vector (Herrera 2026, negative result).

differences.what: Narrative of the search path (what other approaches were tried and failed before landing on the task-identity contrast) relative to White-Bear Steering as the starting reference point
differences.message_quote: What failed (all orthogonal to WBS, all flat or harmful at every dose): answer-time naming, pending-task mode, anaphoric referent-hold (writing and reading registers), register contrast (naming vs circumlocution), and even a named-concept hold over a neutral carrier.

rationale: The write-up names White-Bear Steering only once, in its Novelty paragraph, purely to distinguish the submitted method conceptually ('Not a stance direction...') from it, without any mention of having actually run or reproduced it. The message, by contrast, describes an explicit empirical step of reproducing WBS's recipe as a diagnostic control (reporting a 0.42 score and explaining what it validated about server semantics) and frames the whole search as starting from and diverging away from that baseline — material detail about engagement with the source that the write-up omits entirely, while both documents agree the final submitted method is a distinct task-identity contrast rather than a reproduction of WBS.
